hook: The Emperor Who Sold His Own Palace Treasures
text: Around the year one hundred and seventy, Rome was at war on its northern frontier, and the treasury was almost empty. According to later Roman accounts, the emperor Marcus Aurelius did not want to burden the provinces with heavy new taxes. So for two months, in the Forum of Trajan, he held a great public sale. Gold and crystal cups, statues and paintings, silk robes embroidered with gold, even the jewels of the empress, were sold to pay for the war. Afterwards, the story goes, anyone who wished could return what they had bought and have their money back. No one was forced.
